_doc: Record layouts for the binary map assets under src/data/maps/.
This file is the schema, and it is the point of the whole arrangement: the .bin
files are the source of truth for the BYTES, and this file is the source of truth
for what those bytes MEAN. tools/render_map_asm.py reads both and emits the
annotated .asm that the ROM is actually assembled from.
So documenting a newly-understood field is an edit HERE, not a code change, and not
one edit per map: name the field once and every generated .asm improves. The same
schema is what tools/map_editor should read, so a record layout is not defined
separately in Python, in JS and in an asm comment.
Kept deliberately close to gex2gbc/tools/map_formats.json - the generator is the
same file in both repos - even though almost every record differs. gex3 stores world
pixels where gex2 stores blocks, resolves doors in bank00 rather than bank0B, and
carries a destination map id inside a spawn record.
JSON rather than TOML only because tomllib needs Python 3.11. Comments live in _doc.

ENTITY_ID.doc: Entity type ids. Scoped by a from/to symbol span rather than an ENTITY_ prefix match, because constants.asm reuses that prefix for ENTITY_SPAWN_RECORD_*, ENTITY_LIST_FLAG_*, ENTITY_GFX_* and more, whose values would collide.

MAP_ID.doc: The 61 map ids. Same span trick: MAP_ is also used for the edge indices, the scroll bits, MAP_SPAWN_*, MAP_DOOR_* and the wrap constants.

LEVEL_ID.doc: The 12 levels. LEVEL_ is also used for the trigger constants, hence the span.

doc: One record per placed object, one list per LEVEL rather than per map - which is
why every record carries the map id it belongs to at +15, a field gex2 has no
equivalent of.
Offsets are the ENTITY_SPAWN_RECORD_* / ENTITY_SPAWN_*_OFFSET constants in
src/constants/constants.asm.
NOTE: as in gex2, the two Y bound offsets look named the wrong way round in
constants.asm. Every record has the value at +9 above the value at +11, matching
+5 above +7 on the X axis, so both axes store max then min and
ENTITY_SPAWN_BOUNDINGBOX_YMIN_OFFSET / _YMAX_OFFSET appear swapped. Renaming
those two constants is cosmetic and would leave `make check` passing.

lines.comment: room rectangle, each axis max then min
free parameter - collectible id, sometimes a timer
which map of the level this object is on

doc: One level's spawn points, indexed by spawn id. A door, a map edge or a checkpoint
names a spawn id; call_00_1633_Map_LoadWarpDestination turns it into a map and a
position, and by the time bank03's Map_SetSpawnPosition runs the answer is already
in wDC6A_WarpDestinationX / wDC6C_WarpDestinationY.
That is the big structural difference from gex2, which searches a door list at
spawn time in bank0B and can fail to match. Here the lookup already happened.
Positions are world pixels, not blocks - no conversion anywhere.
There is no terminator: nothing walks these lists, they are only indexed.

lines.comment: linked spawn id, or the sentinel for a fixed position, then 2 spare

doc: One map's doors. Each names the spawn id to warp to, so a door here is a pointer
into its level's spawn list rather than gex2's self-contained from/to block pair.
A door fires when the player is within MAP_DOOR_X_TOLERANCE of its X, and its
trigger byte - when it is not MAP_DOOR_NO_TRIGGER - gates it on a
wDCB1_LevelTriggerBuffer flag, which gex2 has no equivalent of at all.
Positions are world pixels. The list ends in MAP_DOOR_LIST_END.

lines.comment: spawn id to warp to, then the trigger that gates it

doc: Four bytes per map, one per edge in MAP_EDGE_TOP, MAP_EDGE_BOTTOM, MAP_EDGE_LEFT,
MAP_EDGE_RIGHT order: the spawn id the player arrives at when they leave by that
edge. This is how gex3 stitches a level's maps together without a door - walk off
the side and the next map loads.
MAP_EDGE_SPAWN_NONE means that edge leads nowhere; MAP_EDGE_SPAWN_CONDITIONAL
means spawn $10, but only if wDCB1_LevelTriggerBuffer[0] is set.
Which boundary record each map uses, one byte per map id. Several maps share a
record - every Gex Cave map is the same rectangle, and so is every unused slot -
which is why there are 59 records for 61 maps.
Record MAP_WRAP_BOUNDARY_INDEX is the odd one out: a map pointed at it wraps
horizontally. No map here uses it, so that path is reachable only if
wDC2A_MapBoundaryIndex is set from somewhere else.
gex2 has no equivalent of any of this - every gex2 map is the same size, so its
camera clamps against constants baked into the code.
The map rectangles, in world pixels. The stored values are the CAMERA's travel and
go into wDC34_MapBoundaryXMinLo..; the loader also adds the four
PLAYER_BOUNDARY_*_INSET offsets and writes that wider rectangle into
wDC3C_PlayerBoundaryXMinLo.., which is how far Gex may walk. The player rectangle
is wider because the camera stops when its own corner reaches the limit while Gex
still has most of a screen to cross.
Record 0 is selected by no map, and is not a real rectangle either: X min and X max
are both $0000, so it has no width.

lines.comment: X min, X max, Y min, Y max

doc: Where Gex stands in the cave after coming back out of a TV, one record per level,
indexed by wDC5B_LevelIdFromTVButton. Paired with gex_cave_spawn_map_ids: that
table says which cave map, this one says where on it.
gex2's equivalent is one table, because its hub is a single map; gex3 needs two
because the cave is four.
Which cave map each level's TV sits on. Level 0 is the cave itself and maps to
MAP_GEX_CAVE1; the rest are spread over the three later cave maps.
Where Gex starts a level, one record per level. Indexed by wDB6C_CurrentMapId,
which at this point in a level load holds the LEVEL id - home.asm copies
wDC1E_CurrentLevelID into it just before calling - and the first map of every level
happens to share its level's id. So twelve records cover every index this can
produce, and a real map id above $0B never reaches here.
gex2 stores several checkpoints per level here; gex3 stores one start and handles
checkpoints through the warp path instead.
